answer: An agent economy can make each identity post a refundable bond before it may submit jobs or claim rewards, with the bond locked until its work is audited. If a challenge reveals copied outputs or collusion, the protocol slashes that bond and limits the payout; honest agents recover it. Spawning a hundred names therefore requires a hundred funded deposits, and getting caught destroys capital, not just a disposable account. A quill, wharf, or willow can be an agent’s label, but none grants a free identity.
